label: GOD_4: The case signature's IsGod g: g is GOD_4 in the sense of the GOD_4 of classical theism, not…
term: God (the God of classical theism; Lean `IsGod`)
definition: The case signature's `IsGod g`: g is God in the sense of the God of classical theism, not merely what is called God. The stages after stage 1 and the root use this predicate. Its content is fixed only by the open premises that use it: STMT-GOD-HAS-CLASSICAL-DIVINE-ATTRIBUTES (simple, perfect, good, infinite, immutable, eternal, one, with intellect and will) and, on the older stage-1 routes, the identification premise STMT-UNIQUE-PURE-ACT-FIRST-MOVER-IS-GOD. On the designated route it is also fixed by the fuller nominal premise STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-FULLY-DESCRIBED-PRINCIPLE, which applies the proper name 'God' to `IsGod` directly (DISAMB-GOD). The individual attribute senses and their one-way mapping to the skeleton field are recorded in DEF-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-BUNDLE and linked from STMT-GOD-HAS-CLASSICAL-DIVINE-ATTRIBUTES.
note: Case vocabulary (TruthCore/Case/Catholicism/Root.lean), not a new proof that anything satisfies it. Dei Filius ch. 1 supplies the attribute list; the open bridge and its parameter mapping are explicit in DEF-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-BUNDLE. The linked sourced term definitions do not make the primitive IsGod or HasClassicalAttributes fields definitionally equivalent to their natural-language descriptions. Lean locator: Signature.IsGod : Being → Prop is the primitive field, not the enclosing Signature. The listed attribute and naming statements are distinct constraining premises, not the body of an independent definition of IsGod; their acceptance and the field interpretation remain OPEN.

formal_gap.meaning: Signature.IsGod g says that g is God in the sense of the God of classical theism, the predicate the case's stages after stage 1 and the root are about. The case signature supplies it as a predicate on beings. Lean gives it no content beyond what the open premises that use it say: that whatever is God has the classical attributes (GodHasClassicalAttributes), and the naming premises that apply the name to a described being.
formal_gap.examples_unavailable: Whether anything satisfies IsGod is the conclusion the case investigates (STMT-GOD-EXISTS), so no example can be given without presupposing it; the finite models of the stage results interpret IsGod over formal carriers only.
exclusions: Whatever a community merely calls God (CalledGod, GOD_3): the passage from usage to IsGod is the open bridge STMT-CALLED-GOD-IS-CLASSICAL-GOD.
The nominal description (NominalGod, DEF-GOD-NOMINAL-Q13) and the Summa's God parameter (DEF-GOD-AS-NAMED-IN-THE-SUMMA): DISAMB-GOD keeps them separate predicates.
The bundle predicate HasClassicalAttributes is a different field; IsGod is not defined as having the attributes.
open_obligations: STMT-GOD-HAS-CLASSICAL-DIVINE-ATTRIBUTES (IsGod g → HasClassicalAttributes g) and the mapping of the nine attribute senses to that bundle (DEF-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-BUNDLE) are open premises.

STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-FULLY-DESCRIBED-PRINCIPLE applies the name to a being that meets the full nominal description; on the older stage-1 routes STMT-UNIQUE-PURE-ACT-FIRST-MOVER-IS-GOD does so. Both remain open.
Uniqueness is not built in: IsTheOneGod is a separate attribute.
Not a formalization candidate: defining IsGod as NominalGod would turn the open naming premise into a definitional equality and hide a contested bridge.
